data.long_meaning: Murlidhar is a Sanskrit name derived from 'Murlidhara', which means 'God's protector'. This name is associated with Lord Krishna, who is believed to protect his devotees. The name is also a reflection of one's duty and responsibility towards the divine and society. The name Murlidhar carries the meaning “God's protector” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Murlidhar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Murlidhar holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is a name of reverence and devotion to Lord Krishna. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is regarded as the God of protection, and the protector of the universe. The name Murlidhar is a constant reminder of the protective nature of the divine and the responsibility of individuals to seek and maintain the grace of God.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Murlidhar has deep significance for those who bear it. It is a constant reminder of one's spiritual responsibility to protect and uphold the divine principles of love, truth, and righteousness. The name Murlidhar signifies the presence of God within, and the duty to protect and serve the divine in all beings. It serves as a reminder to lead a virtuous life, and to seek the divine grace and protection always.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Murlidhar symbolizes the divine charioteer, guiding us on our spiritual journey towards Krishna, the supreme divine consciousness. The name embodies the faith in Krishna's guidance and the pursuit of inner wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Murlidhar was a popular name for the incarnation of Lord Krishna among the Vaishnavites in medieval India.
historical_references.context: Murlidhar was a revered name for Lord Krishna during the Bhakti movement in medieval India. The Bhakti movement emphasized the devotional love of God, and Murlidhar was considered an embodiment of Krishna's divine love and mercy.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Murlidhar is also the name of a celebrated Jain Tirthankara who lived around the 8th century BCE. The name Murlidhar carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Murlidhar is also known as Mahavira and is considered the last of the 24 Tirthankaras in Jainism. He renounced worldly life and underwent severe ascetic practices, ultimately attaining enlightenment and teaching the path to salvation.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
